incident_description:
my kwikset 99380-001 halo wi-fi smart lock keyless entry electronic keypad deadbolt melted and burned the tips of two of my fingers on sept 23, 2021.
on the late evening of sept 22, 2021 i was in the laundry room that has a door to the garage and i thought i smelled a faint smell of something odd, like a sort of burnt toast.   i checked all around and could not find the smell and it went away.   the following day the kwikset door lock in this room alerted us that its battery was dead and needed replacing.   later on sept 23, 2021 i removed the battery pack from the lock housing and replaced all three 1.5 volt aa batteries, then reinstalled the battery pack .  i then went to verify the locks operation and the lock would illuminate but would not lock or unlock.  then i started to smell a strong smell of something burning and i could see smoke emanating from the just installed battery pack.   i tried to remove the battery pack from the lock housing by lifting up on the plastic removal tab, as i had done previously, it is at this point i burnt my finger tips on the molten plastic.   i then went to the garage and got a dental pick to pull the battery pack out.  once the battery pack was removed the battery pack stopped melting and smoking.   
my fingers were sore but ok, no lasting damage.   
i then notified kwikset about what just happened and uploaded pictures to them using their online tool.  
i asked kwikset if there were any recalls on this product and they said no and there were no know issues. they issued me a case number and said they wanted the complete assembly returned to them for analysis using the prepaid label they provided.
they told me they were sending me a identical replacement as soon as they reviewed the pictures.
i am concerned for several reasons:
- my fingers got burned.
- i do not know what would have happened if i was not home and this happened as the door to the garage is a light wood door.  i do not know if the plastic in the battery pack and cover would ignite or just melt.
- i do not know if the plastic just melted could it have melted and jammed the locking mechanism making it impossible to exit or enter via this door.
- at the time i purchased the kwikset lock that failed i purchased an identical lock, only difference is the color, and installed it in another door.

- There are nodules on the handle to help with grip as well.
- Each brush comes with a plastic cap for storage/travel.
- For a child, the "pocket" between the teeth is perfect for a pea sized amount of toothpaste.
- 4 toothbrushes per pack so if you have one person, you have all that you need for a year if you change every 3 months as recommended.

This is the second time I've purchased this product. I'd purchased brand previously, and the handles were much less substantial, and those didn't come with a cap to cover the brush. So this brand is a much better value for me. I did not receive a discount for this review, these are my personal unbiased opinions.

title: WET ONES Sensitive Skin Moist Wipes Extra Gentle 40 Each (Pack of 9)
incident_description:
this is an email i sent to wet ones customer support: "hello, i would like to tell you about my recent experience with my wet ones sensitive 40 count hand wipes container. i bought two of these containers because they were on my daughters school shopping list and i picked up an extra to try in the car. i had not bought these before then. just this past weekend i tried it out for the first time. after pulling out one wipe, it did not continue to feed so i tried to fix it by pushing a wipe back through the slits on the top. when i did this i accidentally pushed my finger too far through the opening and got my finger stuck right below the base of my cuticle on the skin. it was incredibly painful and like having my finger stuck in a horrible chinese finger trap. i tried to pull my finger back out, but that made the slits dig into my finger even more. i was crying out in pain begging my husband to help me get it off my finger. he somehow managed to get his finger under one of the corners so i had just enough room to get the container off my finger. i have never had such a terrible experience with a wipes container. i buy baby wipes normally and those containers do not have any sharp pokey corners like this container has. what worries my more is that what if a child were to try to fix the feed on the top and get their hand stuck too? it's been two days and i still have a small red indent where the corner stuck in my skin below the cuticle, ouch!! what makes this all the more frustrating is that even after we fixed the feed, almost every time we take a wipe out the next wipe doesn't feed properly anyway so we have to keep fixing it.please rethink the design on this container!"  

this is what i got in reply "... it is indicated on the canister to not push your finger through the opening. we apologize for any trouble you experienced." 

in my opinion, even if they write on the container not to stick your finger through, it is too easy to accidentally push ones finger through and get it stuck. the threading portion of this container is way too sharp for what it is intended to do.

on the late evening of sept 22, 2021 i was in the laundry room that has a door to the garage and i thought i smelled a faint smell of something odd, like a sort of burnt toast.   i checked all around and could not find the smell and it went away.   the following day the kwikset door lock in this room alerted us that its battery was dead and needed replacing.   later on sept 23, 2021 i removed the battery pack from the lock housing and replaced all three 1.5 volt aa batteries, then reinstalled the battery pack .  i then went to verify the locks operation and the lock would illuminate but would not lock or unlock.  then i started to smell a strong smell of something burning and i could see smoke emanating from the just installed battery pack.   i tried to remove the battery pack from the lock housing by lifting up on the plastic removal tab, as i had done previously, it is at this point i burnt my finger tips on the molten plastic.   i then went to the garage and got a dental pick to pull the battery pack out.  once the battery pack was removed the battery pack stopped melting and smoking.   
my fingers were sore but ok, no lasting damage.   
i then notified kwikset about what just happened and uploaded pictures to them using their online tool.  
i asked kwikset if there were any recalls on this product and they said no and there were no know issues. they issued me a case number and said they wanted the complete assembly returned to them for analysis using the prepaid label they provided.
they told me they were sending me a identical replacement as soon as they reviewed the pictures.
i am concerned for several reasons:
- my fingers got burned.
- i do not know what would have happened if i was not home and this happened as the door to the garage is a light wood door.  i do not know if the plastic in the battery pack and cover would ignite or just melt.
- i do not know if the plastic just melted could it have melted and jammed the locking mechanism making it impossible to exit or enter via this door.
- at the time i purchased the kwikset lock that failed i purchased an identical lock, only difference is the color, and installed it in another door.

title: WET ONES Sensitive Skin Moist Wipes Extra Gentle 40 Each (Pack of 9)
incident_description:
this is an email i sent to wet ones customer support: "hello, i would like to tell you about my recent experience with my wet ones sensitive 40 count hand wipes container. i bought two of these containers because they were on my daughters school shopping list and i picked up an extra to try in the car. i had not bought these before then. just this past weekend i tried it out for the first time. after pulling out one wipe, it did not continue to feed so i tried to fix it by pushing a wipe back through the slits on the top. when i did this i accidentally pushed my finger too far through the opening and got my finger stuck right below the base of my cuticle on the skin. it was incredibly painful and like having my finger stuck in a horrible chinese finger trap. i tried to pull my finger back out, but that made the slits dig into my finger even more. i was crying out in pain begging my husband to help me get it off my finger. he somehow managed to get his finger under one of the corners so i had just enough room to get the container off my finger. i have never had such a terrible experience with a wipes container. i buy baby wipes normally and those containers do not have any sharp pokey corners like this container has. what worries my more is that what if a child were to try to fix the feed on the top and get their hand stuck too? it's been two days and i still have a small red indent where the corner stuck in my skin below the cuticle, ouch!! what makes this all the more frustrating is that even after we fixed the feed, almost every time we take a wipe out the next wipe doesn't feed properly anyway so we have to keep fixing it.please rethink the design on this container!"  

this is what i got in reply "... it is indicated on the canister to not push your finger through the opening. we apologize for any trouble you experienced." 

in my opinion, even if they write on the container not to stick your finger through, it is too easy to accidentally push ones finger through and get it stuck. the threading portion of this container is way too sharp for what it is intended to do.

- my fingers got burned.

text: I was curious, so these became stocking stuffers this Christmas.  Of course, Santa put one in my stocking as well.  I love the idea behind the design and I've wondered many times why toothbrushes weren't made in a shape like this.  Then I found these, and I thought, "finally!".  But, as cool as they are, it's hard to maneuver in your mouth. The end tip is wide, to accommodate the wrap around bristles, and when I brush (and other family members) the large end tip hits into your back gums when you try to get the back teeth.  Maybe with more use I will be able to handle it better.  But I don't know if that's even possible with the end tip the way it is.  Of note: in the center of the two brush sides is another little brush, for the tops of teeth.  I don't know if it's sufficient in size to get the entire tops of the teeth.  I move the toothbrush around to scrub everywhere well.  I think it's worth the money just to try them, and see if you like them.

my fingers were sore but ok, no lasting damage.   
i then notified kwikset about what just happened and uploaded pictures to them using their online tool.  
i asked kwikset if there were any recalls on this product and they said no and there were no know issues. they issued me a case number and said they wanted the complete assembly returned to them for analysis using the prepaid label they provided.
they told me they were sending me a identical replacement as soon as they reviewed the pictures.
i am concerned for several reasons:
- my fingers got burned.
- i do not know what would have happened if i was not home and this happened as the door to the garage is a light wood door.  i do not know if the plastic in the battery pack and cover would ignite or just melt.
- i do not know if the plastic just melted could it have melted and jammed the locking mechanism making it impossible to exit or enter via this door.
- at the time i purchased the kwikset lock that failed i purchased an identical lock, only difference is the color, and installed it in another door.

on the late evening of sept 22, 2021 i was in the laundry room that has a door to the garage and i thought i smelled a faint smell of something odd, like a sort of burnt toast.   i checked all around and could not find the smell and it went away.   the following day the kwikset door lock in this room alerted us that its battery was dead and needed replacing.   later on sept 23, 2021 i removed the battery pack from the lock housing and replaced all three 1.5 volt aa batteries, then reinstalled the battery pack .  i then went to verify the locks operation and the lock would illuminate but would not lock or unlock.  then i started to smell a strong smell of something burning and i could see smoke emanating from the just installed battery pack.   i tried to remove the battery pack from the lock housing by lifting up on the plastic removal tab, as i had done previously, it is at this point i burnt my finger tips on the molten plastic.   i then went to the garage and got a dental pick to pull the battery pack out.  once the battery pack was removed the battery pack stopped melting and smoking.   
my fingers were sore but ok, no lasting damage.   
i then notified kwikset about what just happened and uploaded pictures to them using their online tool.  
i asked kwikset if there were any recalls on this product and they said no and there were no know issues. they issued me a case number and said they wanted the complete assembly returned to them for analysis using the prepaid label they provided.
they told me they were sending me a identical replacement as soon as they reviewed the pictures.
i am concerned for several reasons:
- my fingers got burned.
- i do not know what would have happened if i was not home and this happened as the door to the garage is a light wood door.  i do not know if the plastic in the battery pack and cover would ignite or just melt.
- i do not know if the plastic just melted could it have melted and jammed the locking mechanism making it impossible to exit or enter via this door.
- at the time i purchased the kwikset lock that failed i purchased an identical lock, only difference is the color, and installed it in another door.

review_title: Great for kids with special needs!
text:
I work with a lot of kids and adults with special needs and also have a sister who has Angelman's Syndrome. About 99% of the individuals I work with HATE oral care and fight against it every step of the way. I have used these toothbrushes with many of my clients and just recently purchased some for my sister. I'm so pleased with them!

First, it is much easier to get these toothbrushes into their mouths, which are usually almost clamped shut. Second, it is much easier to move them around the mouth to reach all the teeth (even the very back ones) since the toothbrush head is somewhat smaller than a regular toothbrush. Third, since implementing the use of these toothbrushes my clients' dentists have been very impressed with the improvement of the cleanliness of the teeth and gums. This is very good news for people who must be both sedated and held down/put on a papoose board in order to have any dental work done.

I should mention that if you buy these for someone who often bites down on the toothbrush, it may need to be replaced more often than a regular toothbrush ( like every 2-3 months) due to the damage of the head and bristles. That being said, these things are pretty darn durable!

Cleaner teeth -> less time in the dental chair -> Less emotional and physical stress on both patients and caregivers -> greater happiness for everyone involved. If you care for anyone with special needs and are questioning whether or not to invest in this product, just do it. It is sooo worth the investment.

incident_description:
my kwikset 99380-001 halo wi-fi smart lock keyless entry electronic keypad deadbolt melted and burned the tips of two of my fingers on sept 23, 2021.
on the late evening of sept 22, 2021 i was in the laundry room that has a door to the garage and i thought i smelled a faint smell of something odd, like a sort of burnt toast.   i checked all around and could not find the smell and it went away.   the following day the kwikset door lock in this room alerted us that its battery was dead and needed replacing.   later on sept 23, 2021 i removed the battery pack from the lock housing and replaced all three 1.5 volt aa batteries, then reinstalled the battery pack .  i then went to verify the locks operation and the lock would illuminate but would not lock or unlock.  then i started to smell a strong smell of something burning and i could see smoke emanating from the just installed battery pack.   i tried to remove the battery pack from the lock housing by lifting up on the plastic removal tab, as i had done previously, it is at this point i burnt my finger tips on the molten plastic.   i then went to the garage and got a dental pick to pull the battery pack out.  once the battery pack was removed the battery pack stopped melting and smoking.   
my fingers were sore but ok, no lasting damage.   
i then notified kwikset about what just happened and uploaded pictures to them using their online tool.  
i asked kwikset if there were any recalls on this product and they said no and there were no know issues. they issued me a case number and said they wanted the complete assembly returned to them for analysis using the prepaid label they provided.
they told me they were sending me a identical replacement as soon as they reviewed the pictures.
i am concerned for several reasons:
- my fingers got burned.
- i do not know what would have happened if i was not home and this happened as the door to the garage is a light wood door.  i do not know if the plastic in the battery pack and cover would ignite or just melt.
- i do not know if the plastic just melted could it have melted and jammed the locking mechanism making it impossible to exit or enter via this door.
- at the time i purchased the kwikset lock that failed i purchased an identical lock, only difference is the color, and installed it in another door.
